Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

water — the clear liquid we drink. Example: Drink a lot of water.
ocean — a very large sea. Example: The ocean is bigger than the lake.
river — water that flows to the sea. Example: There is a river near the town.
lake — a large area of water with land around it. Example: We swim in the lake.
sea — the salt water near the coast. Example: The sea is blue.
clean — not dirty. Example: We need clean water.
fresh — recent and not old. Example: I buy fresh fruit.
salt — a white substance from the sea. Example: The ocean is salt water.
drink — liquid you take in. Example: We drink fresh water.
save — to keep for later, not waste. Example: We should save water.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• Water is everywhere.
• The ocean is bigger than ...
• We drink fresh water.
• It is salt water.
• We should save water.

Reading: read the text and answer the questions.
Water is everywhere: in the ocean, in rivers and in lakes. We drink fresh water, not salt water. Clean water is more important than anything.
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.
A: Where can we find water? B: In rivers, lakes and the ocean. A: Can we drink ocean water? B: No, it is salt water.
Speaking: Pair and group tasks: Discuss why clean water is important and how to save it.
